policies.text: Review contract: current GitView repository membership/source contexts require management by GitHub. GitHubRepository names this contextual contract on the same Repository, not a new identity or a globally inferred implementation. Compiler relations used for membership/source links do not establish actor-action-derived relation occurrences.

Candidate fields are optional partial projections, not complete entity snapshots or creation requirements. Missing is not zero, false, empty, unchanged, or not applicable. Counts are nonnegative when known; enum/range/availability/freshness semantics need separate specifications and are not enforced by scalar typing. No identity from the implicit generated id is adopted as the source/project key.

A Project contains one or more GitHub-managed Repositories. The same Repository can be a member of multiple Projects, including Projects containing repositories from different GitHub organizations. By default one Project corresponds to one Repository. These are product membership rules; they do not identify an actor for every historical membership or prescribe the mechanics of creating default Projects.

Within the same GitHub instance, matching numeric REST repository IDs identify the same Repository; rename and transfer preserve its history and Project memberships. A different numeric ID denotes a different Repository even at an earlier address. HTTP 404 does not establish the current state and must not erase the last known Repository or its memberships. Local key encoding and cross-instance matching remain open.
